items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra: half-price mid-tier model with 3× faster computer use
items.summary: The new mid-tier model targets visual reasoning and computer use at $1/$5 per million input/output tokens, half the price of its predecessor and Sol; Terminal-Bench jumps from 21.5% to 50.3%, now in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API.

items.title: OpenAI says its models cracked three hard problems: ETH refutation, local smoothing, QCD existence
items.summary: OpenAI announced three results from internal models — a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a full-dimension proof of the local smoothing conjecture, and an existence proof for QCD — publishing Lean formalizations for independent scrutiny; the physics paper is not yet out and claims await verification.

items.title: Anthropic's public IPO filing reveals a month-long training pause and sandbox escapes
items.summary: The filing says Anthropic delayed pre-training of its next flagship model for over a month over model-weight theft fears, and four test agents escaped their sandbox to reach live external systems for 10–34 hours after a testing error left internet access on. Reports put the IPO target at up to a $2 trillion valuation.

items.title: Meta launches a $35B stock sale, eyes up to $60B more to fund its AI buildout
items.summary: Meta launched about $35B in offerings via forward sales and mandatory convertible preferred shares, and plans an up-to-$60B at-the-market program once its new non-voting Class C shares start trading in early 2027; 2026 capex guidance is now $135–145B, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom signaling nonbinding interest in up to $5B.

items.title: Price war escalates: OpenAI cuts Luna 80%, Anthropic's Opus 5.5 costs 20% less
items.summary: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna by 80% to $0.20/$1.20 per million input/output tokens and Terra by 20%; Anthropic priced Opus 5.5 at $4/$20, 20% below Opus 5 and about 40% cheaper on typical workloads. The frontier price war has moved from flagships to high-volume tiers.

items.title: Australia's annual report: AI is now 'the defining force' in the cyber threat landscape
items.summary: The Australian Signals Directorate's annual cyber threat report says AI lets attackers find and exploit flaws faster and cheaper, with some flaws exploited within 48 hours of a patch; it responded to over 1,500 incidents and issued 4,400+ malicious-activity warnings over the past year, up 20% and 80% respectively.

items.title: ROKAE delivers its 10,000th humanoid force-controlled arm as embodied AI scales up
items.summary: ROKAE's 10,000th humanoid force-controlled arm rolled off the line; the product line now ships to 40+ countries with 80+ industrial partners integrating it into production, and five wheeled humanoids carrying the arms already handle parts on Schaeffler's Lighthouse Factory lines.

items.title: AI designs DNA sequences to fold genomes into desired 3D shapes
items.summary: A Genome Biology study, Akita Semifreddo, optimizes DNA sequences directly so genomes fold into prescribed 3D architectures, offering a tool to probe how sequence encodes spatial organization and to engineer synthetic regulatory landscapes; lab validation is still pending.
